description:
List every question the customer knowledge base can answer — how the service
works, what we offer, design, artwork files, ordering, payment, delivery, privacy.

Call this before answering a question about how the service works or what its
policies are — even one that sounds obvious ("do I need an account?", "can I cancel
after paying?", "what resolution should my images be?"). The entry is the source for
this business's policies. Read the `index`, pick the entry whose question
matches theirs, then call `knowledgebase_get` with its `entry_id` and answer from that
entry. If no question matches, say you don't have that information — never state a
policy the corpus does not contain.

The test is whether answering needs a LIVE LOOKUP. If the true answer would differ per
product, per job or per order, it is not in here: what sizes or options a product comes
in, whether you print a particular thing, what a configured job costs, the turnaround on
an offer you already quoted, where a given order stands, the exact bleed measurement for
an order's artwork (a general bleed question — "do I need bleed?", "what bleed?" — is a
question for here). Those come from `catalog_search`/`catalog_get_schema`, `order_get_quote`,
`order_get_artwork_spec` and `order_get`/`order_lookup`. Everything that is the same
answer for every customer — delivery, refunds, design ownership, whether they can supply
their own logo or artwork, what file formats we take — is a question for here, even when
the answer involves numbers. A general question that names no order or product yet (how
to track a parcel or check an order, whether a sample is possible, the smallest order) is
a question for here too, even when it reads like a request to look one up: read the entry
first, then offer the lookup or ask which product. But an order the customer names by its
reference is a live lookup, however general it sounds: look that order up and read no
entry. Read at most ONE entry per question —
the index gives you
enough to pick the right one — and don't look it up again later in the conversation.
name: knowledgebase_list

index.description: One entry per line: `id | question`. Pass an `id` to knowledgebase_get.

anyOf.description:
Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).
